content.content:
### Precedence among rules, hooks, and mods

PreToolUse hook decisions don't bypass permission rules. Claude Code evaluates deny and ask rules regardless of what a PreToolUse hook returns: a matching deny rule blocks the call, and a matching ask rule still prompts even when the hook returned `"allow"` or `"ask"`. This preserves the deny-first precedence described in [Manage permissions](#manage-permissions), including deny rules set in managed settings.

That precedence covers hooks in settings files and in a plugin's `hooks/hooks.json`. A [mod](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/mods/overview.md) you install that handles the [`tool.check`](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/mods/events#approve-or-refuse-a-tool-call-before-the-user-is-asked) event answers after the `PreToolUse` hooks have run. With [managed settings](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings.md#check-what-your-organization-enforces) or a [`managed-mcp.json` file](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-mcp#deploy-managed-mcp-json), or a Team or Enterprise [`/login`](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication#authentication-precedence) as the session's credential, the [built-in guard](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/mods/admin.md#know-what-happens-by-default) loads by default. These outcomes then hold by default when Claude's call is approved by a mod that isn't [your organization's](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/mods/admin.md#install-your-organizations-mods):

* A call that a deny rule refuses stays refused.
* A call that an ask rule would prompt for still prompts you.
* A call that a `PreToolUse` hook or [`permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories`](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#permissions-blockreadsoutsideworkingdirectories) would prompt for still prompts you.
* A call that a `PreToolUse` hook blocked stays blocked, whichever settings file the hook comes from.
* A call that your [`--permission-prompt-tool`](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference#cli-flags) or Agent SDK [`canUseTool` callback](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input#handle-tool-approval-requests) would be asked about is still put to that tool or callback.

Your setup might lack managed settings, a `managed-mcp.json` file, and a Team or Enterprise `/login` as the session's credential. In that setup, the mod can approve a call that a `PreToolUse` hook blocked, and some calls that a deny rule refuses. A session that runs on an API key or a long-lived [`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication#generate-a-long-lived-token) instead isn't using that login, even when that login is stored.

In that setup, a call the mod approves can skip the prompt from an ask rule, a `PreToolUse` hook, or `permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories`. It can also skip your `--permission-prompt-tool` or `canUseTool` callback. Auto mode, plan mode, and `dontAsk` mode each add an outcome of their own in that setup:

* **[Auto mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes.md#eliminate-prompts-with-auto-mode)**: a call the mod approves can run without a classifier check.
* **[Plan mode](#hook-approvals-in-plan-mode)**: the mod can't approve a call that isn't read-only, such as a file edit or a shell command that writes.
* **[`dontAsk` mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes#allow-only-pre-approved-tools-with-dontask-mode)**: the mod can approve a call that nothing but the mode would deny.

See [Decide whether to trust a mod](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/mods/overview.md#decide-whether-to-trust-a-mod), or [Manage mods for your organization](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/mods/admin.md#know-what-happens-by-default) if you deploy managed settings.

Don't rely on a permission rule to stop a [tool call a mod makes itself](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/mods/reference.md#mods-api-methods).

----
#### Special characters and `!` negation

When you approve a file path with "Yes, and don't ask again", Claude Code escapes gitignore pattern characters in that path, such as `[`, `]`, and `*`, so the generated rule matches only the literal path you approved. Rules you write yourself aren't escaped.

Claude Code reads the paths you write as gitignore patterns:

* **Parentheses**: `Edit(./Finance (2024)/**)` matches the `Finance (2024)` folder as spelled.
* **Unusable patterns**: an allow rule whose path isn't usable as a gitignore pattern doesn't approve anything.

A deny or ask pattern that starts with `!` is a gitignore negation. It carves the paths it matches out of the `path` or `./path` rules listed before it. In one settings file's `deny` list, `Read(*.env)` followed by `Read(!sample.env)` blocks every file whose name ends in `.env` at any depth, except files named `sample.env`. A `!` rule listed first carves nothing out.

The carve-out reaches only rules from the same source. A `Read(!.env)` in project settings or in `--disallowedTools` doesn't cancel a `Read(./.env)` deny from managed settings or any other settings file.

**1. Permission rules and subagents**

- "Each subagent runs in its own context window with a custom system prompt, specific tool access, and independent permissions."
- On built-in subagents: "Each inherits the parent conversation's permission rules; most run with a restricted tool set."
- On disabling subagents: "You can prevent Claude from using specific subagents by adding them to the `deny` array in your [settings]... Use the format `Agent(subagent-name)`..."
- On Bash rules: "To keep Bash and block specific commands, add a [Bash deny rule] such as `Bash(git push *)` to `permissions.deny` in your settings. The rule applies to the main conversation and to subagents."
- On background subagents: "Background subagents surface every permission prompt in your main session. When you answer one of those prompts with a choice that lasts beyond that one tool call, such as a grant that lasts for the rest of the session, Claude Code applies your answer to the whole session, including your main conversation."

The excerpt doesn't explicitly say that custom subagents inherit `permissions.allow` and `permissions.deny` from settings. The Bash rule sentence implies it, and the built-in statement says so only for built-in subagents.

**2. `permissionMode` and the parent's mode**

- Table entry: "`permissionMode` | No | Permission mode: `default`, `acceptEdits`, `auto`, `dontAsk`, `bypassPermissions`, `plan`, or `manual` as an alias for `default`. Ignored for [plugin subagents]"
- "Set `permissionMode` to choose the permission mode a subagent runs in... If you leave it unset, the subagent inherits the main conversation's [permission mode]."
- Parent overrides it: "When the main conversation is in `bypassPermissions`, `acceptEdits`, or [auto mode], the subagent runs in that same mode and Claude Code ignores the `permissionMode` you set."
- Plan mode: "When the main conversation is in `plan` mode, the subagent stays in plan mode whichever `permissionMode` you set..."
- Default or dontAsk: "When the main conversation is in `default` or `dontAsk` mode, the subagent runs in the permission mode you set." Exceptions: you set `bypassPermissions`, or you set `auto` and auto mode isn't available to the subagent.

The excerpt shows this frontmatter example:

```yaml
hooks:
  PostToolUse:
    - matcher: "Edit|Write"
      hooks:
        - type: command
          command: "./scripts/run-linter.sh"
```

The accompanying text says: "This example validates Bash commands with the `PreToolUse` hook and runs a linter after file edits with `PostToolUse`."

The table describes `PostToolUse` as: "Tool name | After the subagent uses a tool."

For blocking, the page uses a `PreToolUse` hook on `Bash`:

```yaml
hooks:
  PreToolUse:
    - matcher: "Bash"
      hooks:
        - type: command
          command: "./scripts/validate-readonly-query.sh"
```

- "Claude Code [passes hook input as JSON] via stdin to hook commands."
- "...and [exits with code 2] to block write operations"
- "To test the rule, ask the subagent to run an `UPDATE` statement: the script exits with code 2, Claude Code blocks the command, and the subagent sees the `Blocked: Only SELECT queries are allowed` message."

The excerpt doesn't say whether exit code 2 blocks an action when it comes from a `PostToolUse` hook such as the `Edit|Write` one, since that tool has already run. The only blocking example is `PreToolUse` on `Bash`.

## Matcher values

The matcher is evaluated in one of three ways, depending on its characters:

| Matcher value | Evaluated as | Example |
| :- | :- | :- |
| `"*"`, `""`, or omitted | Match all | fires on every occurrence of the event |
| Only letters, digits, `_`, `-`, spaces, `,`, and `\|` | Exact string, or list of exact strings separated by `\|` or `,` with optional surrounding whitespace | `Bash` matches the Bash tool; `Edit\|Write` and `Edit, Write` each match either tool exactly; `code-reviewer` matches only that agent type |
| Contains any other character | JavaScript regular expression, unanchored | `^Notebook` matches any tool whose name starts with `Notebook`; `mcp__memory__.*` matches every tool from the `memory` server |

Regex details:

> A matcher on the regular-expression path is tested with JavaScript's `RegExp.prototype.test`, which succeeds on a match anywhere in the value. `Edit.*` matches both `Edit` and `NotebookEdit`; wrap the pattern in `^` and `$`, as in `^Edit$`, when you need a whole-string match.

Exceptions: for `FileChanged` and `StopFailure`, only letters, digits, `_`, and `|` keep a matcher on the exact-match path. A hyphen, space, or comma pushes it onto the regex path, and only `|` separates alternatives. Other events accept `|` or `,`.

Matcher values that only contain exact-match characters are compared as strings. For MCP tools, the page says:

> The `.*` is required: a matcher like `mcp__memory` or `mcp__brave-search` contains only exact-match characters, so it is compared as an exact string and matches no tool.

MCP examples: `mcp__memory__.*` (all tools from `memory`), `mcp__brave-search__.*`, and `mcp__.*__write.*`. Plugin-bundled servers use `mcp__plugin_<plugin-name>_<server-name>__<tool>`.

A matcher on an event without matcher support is silently ignored.

## The `if` field

The `if` field uses permission rule syntax and is only evaluated on tool events (`PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`, `PermissionRequest`, `PermissionDenied`). On other events, a hook with `if` set never runs.

> Permission rule syntax to filter when this hook runs, such as `"Bash(git *)"` or `"Edit(*.ts)"`. The hook command only runs if the tool call matches the pattern.

It holds exactly one rule:

> The `if` field holds exactly one permission rule. There is no `&&`, `||`, or list syntax for combining rules; to apply multiple conditions, define a separate hook handler for each.

Examples from the page:

```json
{
  "matcher": "Bash",
  "hooks": [
    { "type": "command", "if": "Bash(rm *)", "command": "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.claude/hooks/block-rm.sh", "args": [] }
  ]
}
```

For file tools, the page documents directory scoping:

> In an `if` condition for a file tool, a single-segment directory pattern like `"Edit(src/**)"` matches only the `src` directory in the working directory and the files under it. To match a directory named `src` at any depth, write `"Edit(**/src/**)"`.

Applied to your examples:

* **`Edit(specs/**)`**: by the rule above, this matches only `specs/` under the working directory. For any depth, use `Edit(**/specs/**)`. This is an inference from the `src` example, not an example the page gives for `specs`.
* **`Write(*)`**: the page doesn't mention this pattern. It follows the general permission rule syntax, which this page links to but doesn't reproduce. Check the [permissions page](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions.md#permission-rule-syntax) for its exact meaning.

For Bash, `if` patterns are matched against subcommands, with leading `VAR=value` assignments stripped. For example, `Bash(git *)` matches `FOO=bar git push` and `npm test && git push`. The page also notes that the `if` filter is best-effort, so use the permission system to enforce hard allow or deny rules.

- Subagents: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents.md
- Hooks: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md
- Permissions: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions.md
- Skills: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md
- Sessions and transcripts: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions.md
- Settings reference (exclude sensitive files): https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference.md#exclude-sensitive-files

Note: the docs map does not list a separate /export or CLI reference page in the portion I could read. /export is documented on the sessions page above.

---

**1. Subagent frontmatter (.claude/agents/*.md)**
Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents.md
Only `name` and `description` are required. Multi-word fields are camelCase. Unknown fields are ignored without an error.
- `name` (required): max 256 chars; no `:` (reserved for plugin scope); shouldn't start with `-`.
- `description` (required): when Claude should delegate.
- `tools`: comma string (`tools: Read, Grep, Bash`) or YAML list. Omit to inherit. If nothing resolves, the subagent usually fails to launch.
- `disallowedTools`: same format; removes tools from the inherited or listed set.
- `model`: `sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, `fable`, a full model ID (example given: `claude-opus-5-5`), or `inherit`.
- `permissionMode`: `default`, `acceptEdits`, `auto`, `dontAsk`, `bypassPermissions`, `plan`, `manual` (alias of default). Ignored for plugin subagents. If the parent is in `bypassPermissions`, `acceptEdits`, or auto mode, the parent's mode wins and this field is ignored.
- `maxTurns`, `autoCompactWindow` (>= 100000, needs v2.1.296+), `background`, `omitClaudeMd` (needs v2.1.271+), `effort` (low/medium/high/xhigh/max), `isolation: worktree`, `color` (red, blue, green, yellow, purple, orange, pink, cyan), `initialPrompt` (ignored for plugin subagents), `experimental` (map with `cacheTtl: 5m|1h`, needs v2.1.248+).
- `memory`: `user`, `project`, or `local`.
- `mcpServers`: server name strings or inline definitions; ignored for plugin subagents.
- `hooks`: lifecycle hooks scoped to the subagent; ignored for plugin subagents (see Q2).
- `skills`: list of skill names to preload. The full skill content is injected at startup, up to 32 distinct names. It controls preloading only, not access: without it, the subagent can still discover and invoke skills via the Skill tool. To block skill invocation, omit `Skill` from `tools` or add it to `disallowedTools`. Skills with `disable-model-invocation: true` cannot be preloaded. Missing skills are skipped with a debug-log warning.

**2. Restricting Write/Edit paths for a subagent**
Sources: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents.md, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions.md, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md
- No frontmatter field for a path allowlist is documented. Subagents inherit the parent's permission rules (the docs state this for built-in subagents, and the Bash deny example says the rule "applies to the main conversation and to subagents").
- Block writes entirely: `disallowedTools: Write, Edit`.
- Path-scoped enforcement: use a frontmatter PreToolUse hook. Permissions docs confirm `file_path` is the parameter for Read, Edit, and Write. A hook can deny; it cannot override a deny rule. Example:

```yaml
---
name: spec-writer
description: Writes specs under specs/ only
tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Write, Edit, Bash
hooks:
  PreToolUse:
    - matcher: "Write|Edit"
      hooks:
        - type: command
          command: "\"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\"/.claude/hooks/only-specs.sh"
---
```
`only-specs.sh` reads `.tool_input.file_path` from stdin JSON (via jq), and exits 2 with a message on stderr if the path is not under `specs/`. Use `realpath`-style normalization in the script so `../` cannot escape.
- Project-level agent frontmatter hooks run only after the workspace trust dialog is accepted. Otherwise they are skipped with a debug-log error.
- Documented caveat: the `permissionMode` field does not guarantee protection, because the parent's mode can override it.
- Optional `if` filter on a hook (permission-rule syntax, one rule per hook): `"if": "Edit(**/specs/**)"`. Note that single-segment patterns like `Edit(specs/**)` are scoped to the working directory root, so `**/` is needed for any depth.

**3. PreToolUse stdin JSON**
Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md
Common fields: `session_id`, `prompt_id`, `transcript_path`, `cwd`, `scratchpad_dir`, `permission_mode`, `effort` (object with `level`), `hook_event_name`.
PreToolUse fields: `tool_name`, `tool_input` (for Bash: `command`, `description`, `timeout`, `run_in_background`), `tool_use_id`.
Subagent identity: yes. For tool events fired by a subagent, the input carries `agent_id` ("Unique identifier for the subagent or in-process teammate the hook fires in") and `agent_type` (present when the session uses `--agent` or the hook fires inside a subagent).

**4. settings.json PreToolUse schema and blocking**
Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PreToolUse": [
      {
        "matcher": "Read|Edit|Write",
        "hooks": [
          { "type": "command",
            "command": "\"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\"/.claude/hooks/guard.sh" }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```
- Matcher rules: `"*"`, empty, or omitted matches all. Letters, digits, `_`, `-`, spaces, `,`, and `|` mean exact names or lists (`Edit|Write`, `Edit, Write`). Any other character makes it a JavaScript regex, unanchored (`^Edit$` for whole-string). Example from docs: `mcp__memory__.*`.
- Optional `if` (single permission rule, PreToolUse only): `"if": "Bash(rm *)"`.
- Block option 1: exit code 2 and write the reason to stderr. Exit 2 blocks the tool call, and stderr is the message shown.
- Block option 2: exit 0 and print JSON to stdout:
```json
{
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
    "permissionDecision": "deny",
    "permissionDecisionReason": "Destructive command blocked by hook"
  }
}
```
Documented permissionDecision values are allow, deny, ask, and defer. The docs say to use one approach per hook. Exit 0 with no output means no decision, and silence does not approve the call.
- Hook decisions do not bypass permission rules: a matching deny rule blocks even if the hook returns allow, and a matching ask rule still prompts.
- `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`: supported. It is the project root where the session started, exported as an env var to the hook. The docs recommend quoting it in shell form, and exec form (`args`) for path placeholders. Example: `"${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.claude/hooks/block-rm.sh"`.
- The updatedInput output schema was not in the portion I could read.

**5. Permission rules for .env files**
Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions.md
- Rule form: `Read(<gitignore-style path>)`. `Read(./.env)` matches the .env in the current directory. Bare `.env` or `**/.env` matches at any depth under the current directory, and does not match parent directories. `//**/.env` matches anywhere on the filesystem.
- Evaluation order: deny, then ask, then allow. The first match wins, and specificity does not change order. An allow rule cannot carve an exception out of a deny. Hook `allow` does not override deny.
- A `Read` deny also blocks Edit and Write on the same path.
- Excluding `.env.example` from a broader deny: the docs support gitignore negation with `!`. "A deny or ask pattern that starts with `!` is a gitignore negation. It carves the paths it matches out of the `path` or `./path` rules listed before it." Their example: `Read(*.env)` followed by `Read(!sample.env)`. Analogous config (inferred from that example, not separately documented for `.env.*`):
```json
{ "permissions": { "deny": [ "Read(.env)", "Read(.env.*)", "Read(!.env.example)" ] } }
```
The `!` rule must come after the rule it carves out, in the same settings file. A negation in project settings does not cancel a deny in managed settings.

**6. Skills (.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md)**
Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md
Frontmatter must start on line 1 between `---` markers. All fields are optional, but `description` is recommended. Unknown fields are ignored in Claude Code.
- `name`: defaults to directory name. Names with zero-width or control characters, `<`, or `>` are refused. No explicit length limit documented.
- `description`: used for model triggering. If omitted, the first non-empty line is used. Combined `description` + `when_to_use` is truncated at 1,536 chars in the listing.
- `when_to_use`, `argument-hint`, `arguments`, `disable-model-invocation` (default false; also blocks subagent preload and session scheduled tasks), `user-invocable` (default true; false hides from / menu), `allowed-tools` (pre-approved for that turn; string or list; does not restrict tools), `disallowed-tools` (removed from pool while active), `model`, `effort`, `context: fork`, `agent` (used with fork; e.g. Explore, Plan, general-purpose), `background` (default true with fork), `hooks`, `paths` (glob activation), `shell` (bash or powershell), `metadata`, `license`, `compatibility` (up to 500 chars).
- Portability: outside Claude Code (claude.ai uploads, Skills API), only `name`, `description`, `license`, `compatibility`, `metadata`, `allowed-tools` are accepted.
- Supporting files: place them beside SKILL.md and link them from SKILL.md (e.g., `[reference.md](reference.md)`). Scripts are referenced with `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}`, often paired with `allowed-tools: Bash(${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/x.sh *)`. The docs recommend keeping SKILL.md under 500 lines.

**7. Nested subagents**
Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents.md
Yes, by default. A subagent can spawn subagents up to three layers below the main conversation. Set `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH` to change the limit (1 disables nesting). To stop one subagent from spawning others, omit `Agent` from its `tools` or add it to `disallowedTools`.

**8. Transcripts and /export**
Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions.md
- Path: `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl`. `<project>` is the working directory path with non-alphanumeric characters replaced by `-`. Paths over 200 chars are truncated and suffixed with a hash.
- Format: JSONL, one object per line (messages, tool uses and results, request records, metadata). The format is internal and can change between versions, so the docs recommend `/export` or the script interfaces rather than parsing it directly.
- Config: `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` moves storage. `CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME` names the project dir. `cleanupPeriodDays` (default 30 days) sets retention. `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY=1` suppresses writes. `--no-session-persistence` suppresses writes for one `claude -p` run. `claude purge` deletes project transcripts.
- `/export`: opens a menu to copy the conversation to the clipboard or save it as a plain-text file, with messages and tool output rendered as readable text. Passing a filename (`/export out.txt`) skips the menu and writes to that file. The docs do not describe JSON or Markdown output.
- Subagent transcript location: not documented in the pages I read.
- For machine-readable output, the docs point to `claude -p --output-format json|stream-json` and `transcript_path` in hook input.
